title: Sweat

teacherSummary.text: Delia Jones, a washerwoman in Eatonville, Florida, has supported her abusive husband Sykes for fifteen years. Sykes wants her out of the house for his mistress and terrorizes her with a rattlesnake he keeps in a box. One night the snake gets loose; Sykes, in the dark, is bitten. Delia, hearing his cries, does not help, and waits under the Chinaberry tree as he dies.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “Mah tub of suds is filled yo' belly with vittles more times than yo' hands is filled it” slowly and put it in my own words: Delia tells Sykes that her washtub has fed him more often than his own hands have. Next, craft. I notice the balanced comparison, her tub against his hands. The strongest word is “suds”: it stands for her laundry work, the labor that pays for everything. Then, effect. What is Delia saying about who has supported the household? My answer: Delia is claiming the house and food as hers by right of work; this is the first time she stands up to Sykes.
